title: POC Weekly Sync - Rollout / Go-Live Planning

Reviewed metrics from last week's benchmark (latency, error rate), agreed on canary percentages and monitoring dashboards, clarified rollback triggers and runbook ownership, and defined next steps including updated runbook, SSO smoke test, and a 24-hour canary window for production traffic ramp.

transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-08-05
Time: 11:00am PT
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Samir Patel (Redwood AE), Jenna Ortiz (Redwood SE), Carlos Ng (Redwood SE), Lisa Chen (BrightHealth Head of ML), Marco Ruiz (BrightHealth Platform Eng), Aisha Khan (BrightHealth PM), David Park (BrightHealth SRE)
Shared: canary runbook (draft link), Grafana dashboards, benchmark spreadsheet

Summary (auto-generated): Finalizing cutover/canary plan. Focus on monitoring thresholds, rollback criteria, and operational runbooks.

Transcript:
00:00 Speaker 1 (Samir): All right thanks everyone for joining, um we'll start with a quick recap from last week, then jump into the canary plan. Jenna do you want to kick off with the metrics we saw from the stress runs?
01:02 Jenna (SE): Yeah sure. So the benchmark we ran on Thursday, um the p95 latency for our main prompt set was about 210 millisecond on the dedicated pool, p99 around 320, error rate was 0.6 percent under sustained load. Note there was one flakey instance where the K V cache warmed slowly - transcription sometimes says K V cash - but we tracked it to an instance with older kernel libs. We've reduced that in the next image.
03:18 Lisa (Head of ML): That's great, those numbers look in line with our SLOs. Our main concern is tail latency during the A B test, we can't have significant regressions vs current in-house.
03:45 Jenna: Yeah agreed. We also saw token generation throughput steady for 1k concurrent sessions, and the cache hit rate for prefix caching was about 78 percent on average which helped the cost numbers.
05:10 Marco (Platform): Quick ops note - during the last run we saw a spike in ephemeral GPU memory on one node; Carlos, you mentioned you pinned a kernel change?
05:30 Carlos (Redwood): Yeah we rebuilt that runtime image and pushed the fix to the dedicated pool; should be in the next run. It's a config level mismatch, nothing to do with the model.
06:12 Aisha (PM): From product side we want a canary that runs for at least 24 hours with a slow ramp, and critical business flows smoke-tested each step - payments, patient lookup, and note generation.
06:55 Samir: Ok, so proposed canary steps: 0% baseline, 1% for 1 hour, 5% for 4 hours, 25% for 12 hours, then 50% for 24 hours, if that looks too slow we can accelerate but safety first. Thoughts?
08:12 David (SRE): I like the staged approach, but we need clear rollback triggers - I'm thinking p99 latency > 400ms sustained for 5 minutes, or error rate > 1.5 percent 5min avg, or any data-exfil anomaly. If any of those happen we auto-roll back to previous route.
09:00 Jenna: We'll set alert thresholds in Grafana and hook into your PagerDuty on-call. I'll include playbooks for investigation steps: check infra, tail logs, check KV cache hit, rollback command.
10:30 Lisa: Also want to make sure audit logs for inference requests are captured to satisfy compliance. We need KMS events in the runbook and a note about redwood private if encryption at rest is required.
11:05 Carlos: We already have audit hooks in the private deployment, for hosted we can stream logs to your SIEM; I'll add the specific log fields to the runbook.
12:20 Marco: On networking - cutover requires a short maintenance window for DNS TTL swaps or for traffic routing via load balancer. We'd prefer using canary routing at the gateway rather than DNS. Any problems with that?
13:00 Samir: We recommend smart routing at the load balancer layer; Redwood's control plane can manage canary weights and fall back to regional replicas. We'll document exact curl commands and UI steps in the runbook.
14:10 Aisha: What's the expected rollback time? In worst case, how long till all traffic back to previous variant?
14:40 Jenna: Typically the weight is changed at gateway, so within 30 seconds most traffic is back, but in practice you want to plan for 2-5 minutes for caches to flush and sessions to rebalance. We'll include explicit verification steps.
16:05 David: We need a pre-cutover checklist: SSO smoke test, KMS access, audit log streaming, alert wiring to PD, and runbook owner assigned.
16:40 Samir: Great - we can make a checklist. Who volunteers to own runbook during the canary?
17:02 Lisa: David and I will co-own incident response, Marco will own infra provisioning and smoke test, Aisha will coordinate stakeholders.
17:30 Samir: I'll be the Redwood primary contact and Jenna will be on-call for immediate SE triage. Carlos will be backup.
18:15 Jenna: For monitoring, we propose the following key dashboards: latency (p50/p95/p99), errors by endpoint, throughput, cache hit rate, GPU memory/temperature, and request audit logs sample. I'll share links after call.
19:10 Marco: Can we also set a canary-only synthetic that runs the three critical flows every 5 minutes to give early warning?
19:45 Jenna: Yes, synthetic checks are included, we'll add small load tests and health checks at each step.
20:30 Lisa: Security review - our InfoSec wants to verify SAML SSO works end-to-end, and also want to confirm that on the hosted side, customer data isn't logged beyond request IDs.
21:10 Carlos: On hosted, we redact user-provided PII from logs by default and can enable additional retention policies; for private we can commit to no external logging. We'll note specifics in the security appendix of the runbook.
22:40 Samir: Good. Let's set the go/no-go decision for Monday 2026-08-10 EOD. That gives a few days to iterate on the runbook and run a staging smoke test.
23:10 Aisha: Sounds good. A couple of edge cases: what if we see intermittent errors only in mobile clients? Do we include client-level weights?
24:00 Jenna: We'll route by session cookie and user-agent; canary can be targeted by user segments if needed. We'll include examples: header based routing and session cookie.
25:30 Lisa: One more thing - data residency: some requests must remain in EU region, Redwood routing must respect region policies during canary.
26:00 Samir: Noted. We'll lock region constraints for those routes; they'll be exempt from the global canary unless you want them included.
27:05 David: Runbook should include communications plan - who to notify at each step and escalation matrix.
27:40 Samir: We'll add a communications section with Slack channels and PD but also email list for execs.
28:30 Jenna: I will also add a quick rollback dry-run procedure so on-call can rehearse, short doc: simulate an alert, execute weight shift, validate rollback.
29:20 Marco: For the smoke test creds - I'll provision a short-lived API key scoped to canary environment and share via secure vault.
30:00 Carlos: One translator note - sometimes Fireflies mislabels speakers, so if there are misattributions just flag them.
30:20 Samir: Thanks. Any blockers we haven't captured?
31:00 Lisa: The only outstanding is a SOC2 detail around log retention for audit logs - I'll send a specific ask to Samir after this call.
31:25 Samir: Ok please send, we'll respond with options for retention windows and controls.
32:10 Aisha: OK can we confirm the exact timing for the 24-hour canary? If the 50 percent step lasts 24 hours does that push go-live out by a day?
33:00 Samir: The full planned run would likely be two days end-to-end if we go through the 50 percent step; we can shorten if metrics are green but we want at least a 24 hour window at a meaningful traffic weight like 50 percent to observe production behaviours.
34:20 Jenna: I'll prepare a metric snapshot template for each ramp step so the go/no-go board can look at consistent numbers.
35:00 Samir: Great. To recap next steps: Samir send runbook, Jenna dashboards, Marco staging creds, David validate SSO, and Aisha coordinate stakeholders. Go/no-go scheduled 2026-08-10.
36:10 Lisa: Thanks everyone. Any final Qs?
36:30 Marco: Quick one - do we need a DB migration freeze or anything?
36:50 David: Not for this rollout, it's purely inference routing change; but we will freeze any infra changes during canary window.
37:10 Samir: Ok we'll note a deploy freeze and a small maintenance window in the runbook.
37:40 Aisha: Thanks all.
38:00 Samir: Thanks folks, we'll follow up with the links. Meeting adjourned.

References/links mentioned in call:
- Draft canary runbook: https://redwood.example/runbooks/brighthealth-canary-draft (doc)
- Grafana dashboards (shared in follow-up)
- Benchmark spreadsheet: https://sheets.example/brighthealth-poc-benchmarks
- Security appendix: will be attached to runbook

Explicit next steps (captured):
- Send updated runbook with step timings and rollback criteria (Samir)
- Share dashboards and alert playbooks (Jenna)
- Provision staging VLAN/creds for smoke (Marco)
- SSO/audit log validation in staging (David)
- Stakeholder go/no-go on 2026-08-10 (Aisha/Lisa)

End of transcript.
